Public Accounts Committee

The responsibilities of this Committee include checking whether the various expenditures made by State institutions are made in accordance with legal authorisation and in accordance with the budget passed by the Majlis, and checking whether the amounts of money passed by the Majlis are being spent on those purposes. They also include the Committee examining, where State institutions have spent money beyond the authorised amount, the reasons and circumstances that required such spending. Accordingly, in examining matters relating to the State's finances, the responsibilities include studying the financial accounts of State institutions, State-owned companies, State business enterprises and independent State institutions; studying the various reports of the Auditor General, identifying the measures to be taken and instructing the relevant State institutions. In addition, they include carrying out the matters required in connection with the role the Majlis must play in State borrowing and in the issuing of guarantees by the State; overseeing the work of the Maldives Monetary Authority and the Auditor General's Office; and seeking the advice of other committees in determining the salaries to be determined by the People's Majlis.

1. Introduction

As stated in Article 120(b)(10) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, the responsibilities of the Public Accounts Committee include advising the Majlis on determining the salaries and allowances to be determined by the People's Majlis, and seeking the advice of other relevant committees in determining those salaries. Accordingly, this report is the report on the Committee's study and decision on the matter of reviewing, among the salaries and allowances to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, the salary and allowances of the Speaker of the People's Majlis, the vehicle allowances of members of the Cabinet, and the allowances of island councillors. The schedule included in this report forms part of this report.

2. Documents considered by the Committee in studying the matter

In studying this matter, the Committee considered the following reports.

1. "Report on the decision of the Public Accounts Committee on re-reviewing the matter, following the Majlis's return to the Committee of the report submitted to the Majlis, concluded on 26 August 2010, on the Public Accounts Committee's review/formulation of the salary structure to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution and Article 100(a)(10) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis", passed by the People's Majlis on 28 December 2010;

2. "Report on the decision of the Public Accounts Committee on re-reviewing the salary structure to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution and Article 100(a)(10) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis" (Report No. މލކ/2012/ރ-10), passed by the People's Majlis on 31 December 2012;

3. "Amendment submitted to the report concluded on 25 December 2012 on the Public Accounts Committee's re-review of the salary structure to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution and Article 100(a)(10) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis" (Report No. މލކ/2014/ރ-3), passed by the People's Majlis on 21 July 2014; and

[signature] [stamp]

4. "Report on the review and reformulation of the structure of salaries and allowances to be determined by the People's Majlis" (Report No. M19/ML/2024/01), passed by the People's Majlis on 28 February 2024.

3. How the Committee's work proceeded

The Public Accounts Committee of the People's Majlis has noted that there are disparities in the salaries and allowances currently received by those who receive salaries and allowances to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives. Therefore, at the Committee's 24th meeting held on 21 October 2026, it was decided by a majority of the members present and voting that the Public Accounts Committee would take the initiative to deliberate among members on reviewing those salaries and allowances in order to reduce the disparities in the salaries and allowances received by such posts.

4. How the Committee's deliberations proceeded

At the Committee's 24th meeting held on 21 October 2026, the Committee members deliberated on the following matters.

4.1. Salary and allowances of the Speaker of the People's Majlis

It is noted that the total amount received by the Speaker of the People's Majlis as salary and allowances is less than that of the Deputy Speaker of the People's Majlis and the members of the Majlis. Accordingly, while the Speaker of the People's Majlis currently receives a total of MVR 73,125 (seventy-three thousand one hundred and twenty-five) as salary and allowances, the Deputy Speaker of the People's Majlis currently receives a total of MVR 91,000 (ninety-one thousand) as salary and allowances. A member of the People's Majlis currently receives a total of MVR 82,500 (eighty-two thousand five hundred) as salary and allowances. Therefore, the Committee decided to review the allowances of the Speaker of the People's Majlis, set a special allowance of MVR 22,000 (twenty-two thousand), and set a total of MVR 95,125 (ninety-five thousand one hundred and twenty-five)

[signature] [stamp]

as salary and allowances for the Speaker of the People's Majlis. With this change, it is estimated that an additional MVR 264,000 (two hundred and sixty-four thousand) per year will be spent on the salary and allowances of the Speaker of the People's Majlis over the current expenditure. 4.2. Vehicle allowance of members of the Cabinet

The salaries and allowances of posts to be determined by the People's Majlis have been determined within a framework formulated for that purpose. However, looking at the changes made at various times to the salaries and allowances of those posts, the Committee has noted that posts of a lower grade are receiving higher salaries than the salary received by members of the Cabinet. Accordingly, although the post of a member of the Cabinet is a post of a higher grade than chief judges, judges, chief magistrates and magistrates of the courts, and the heads of independent posts and the presidents of independent institutions are posts of the same grade as members of the Cabinet, the salary received by members of the Cabinet

[signature] [stamp]

is, as the Committee has noted, lower than the salary received by the posts described above. The Committee has also noted that the Chief Justice of the Maldives, the justices of the Supreme Court of the Maldives, the heads of independent posts, the presidents of independent institutions, and the mayors of city councils are receiving vehicle allowances equal to those received by members of the Cabinet. Therefore, the Committee members deliberated on reviewing the vehicle allowances of members of the Cabinet. At present, the vehicle allowances received total MVR 7,500 (seven thousand five hundred), comprising MVR 1,000 (one thousand) as petrol allowance and MVR 6,500 (six thousand five hundred) as drivers' salary. After deliberation in the Committee, the Committee decided to set a total of MVR 17,000 (seventeen thousand) as vehicle allowances, comprising MVR 2,000 (two thousand) as petrol allowance, MVR 12,000 (twelve thousand) as drivers' salary and MVR 3,000 (three thousand) as drivers' living allowance. With this change, it is estimated that an additional MVR 1,710,000 (one million seven hundred and ten thousand) per year will be spent on the vehicle allowances of members of the Cabinet over the current expenditure. 4.3. Allowance of island councillors

Looking at the salaries and allowances of city councillors and island councillors elected under the decentralised system, the Committee has noted that there is a relatively large disparity in those salaries and allowances. Accordingly, while a city council mayor receives a total of MVR 46,000 (forty-six thousand) as salary and allowances, a deputy mayor receives a total of MVR 40,500 (forty thousand five hundred) as salary and allowances. City council members receive a total of MVR 35,000 (thirty-five thousand) as salary and allowances. However, the president of an island council currently receives only a total of MVR 25,500 (twenty-five thousand five hundred) as salary and allowances. While the vice president of an island council currently receives a total of MVR 20,000 (twenty thousand) as salary and allowances, island council members currently receive a total of MVR 18,000 (eighteen thousand) as salary and allowances. Looking at the amounts described above, the Committee has noted that there is a large disparity in the salaries of island council presidents, vice presidents and island council members compared with the salaries of city council mayors, deputy mayors and city council members.

In addition, following the migration of council staff to the State pay framework on 01 November 2025, there has been a positive change in the salaries of council staff. With this change, it has come to the Committee's attention that the salaries of councillors elected by the people to run the people's affairs on the islands on democratic principles are lower than the salaries of administrative staff in some posts at the councils. Therefore, the Committee decided to review the salaries and allowances of island council presidents, vice presidents and island council members. Accordingly, the Committee decided to add MVR 5,000 (five thousand) as a service allowance, in addition to the salary and allowances currently received by island council presidents, vice presidents and island council members. Therefore, with the newly added service allowance, the island council president will receive a total of MVR 30,500 (thirty thousand five hundred)

[signature] [stamp]

as salary and allowances, and the island council vice president will receive a total of MVR 25,000 (twenty-five thousand) as salary and allowances. An island council member will receive a total of MVR 23,000 (twenty-three thousand) as salary and allowances. With this change, it is estimated that an additional MVR 37,560,000 (thirty-seven million five hundred and sixty thousand) per year will be spent on councillors' salaries and allowances over the current expenditure. 5. Committee's decision

Regarding the matter taken up on the initiative of the Public Accounts Committee of the People's Majlis after it noted that there are disparities in the salaries and allowances currently received by those who receive salaries to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, after deliberation at the Committee's 24th meeting of 2026, a majority of the members present decided to pass it with the changes deliberated on and reviewed in the Committee: establishing a special allowance for the Speaker of the People's Majlis, increasing the vehicle allowances of members of the Cabinet, and establishing a service allowance for island council presidents, vice presidents and members.

The proposed date for providing the salaries and allowances with the changes proposed to the salary structure by the People's Majlis is from the day this report is passed on the floor of the People's Majlis.

Therefore, we submit this report to the People's Majlis under Article 120(b)(12) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis for a decision on this report.
